Honestly, I keep thinking they would all be much better off if I just disappeared.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling like a burden and that others would be better off without you, have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you weren't alive?\n\nPatient: Yes, I catch myself thinking it would be easier if my heart would just hurry up and quit. I haven't actually tried anything, but the thoughts are there.\n\nDoctor: Have you lost interest in activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy before these symptoms started, or are you still able to find some pleasure in the things you do?\n\nPatient: I've completely lost interest in everything I used to love, like singing in the church choir and tinkering on my old Chevy in the garage. I just know deep down that my heart is already rotten and doomed, and I believe this illness is God's way of punishing me for all the mistakes I've made in my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how long you've been experiencing these thoughts and hearing the voice, and have they been persistent or have they come and gone over time?\n\nPatient: It's been going on for about four months now, starting a few weeks after my heart diagnosis when I fell into this dark depression. I've never experienced anything like this before in my life, but now it's constant and doesn't really go away, especially at night when the house is quiet.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling like your heart condition is a punishment from God for your past mistakes, can you tell me more about what you mean by that and how often these feelings of guilt overwhelm you?\n\nPatient: I feel like God is punishing me for all my past mistakes, like yelling at my kids years ago or skipping choir rehearsals. This guilt is with me every single day, and I just feel like a useless burden to my wife, my church, and the doctors. Honestly, I keep thinking they would all be much better off if I just disappeared.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling like a burden and that others would be better off without you, have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you weren't alive?\n\nPatient: Yes, I catch myself thinking it would be easier if my heart would just hurry up and quit. I've sat alone in the garage more than once picturing different ways to make sure I don't wake up. I haven't actually tried anything, but the thoughts are there.\n\nDoctor: Have you lost interest in activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy before these symptoms started, or are you still able to find some pleasure in the things you do?\n\nPatient: I've completely lost interest in everything I used to love, like singing in the church choir and tinkering on my old Chevy in the garage. Now, even the thought of picking up a wrench or warming up my voice feels completely pointless and exhausting. Most days I just sit in my recliner staring at the TV with it turned off, letting calls from my buddies go straight to voicemail.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, can you tell me if there are any activities or things that still bring you some pleasure or make you feel slightly better, even if it's just for a little while?\n\nPatient: No, absolutely nothing brings me pleasure or makes me feel better anymore. Even the things I used to live for, like my old Chevy or the choir, just feel completely pointless and exhausting now. Most of the time I just sit in my recliner staring at a blank TV screen, feeling completely empty.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling empty and that nothing brings you pleasure, can you tell me if there was a specific point in time when you noticed this lack of interest and pleasure in activities, or was it a gradual change over the four months since your heart diagnosis?\n\nPatient: It was a gradual slide that started a few weeks after my heart diagnosis, about four months ago. At first, I just stopped going to choir and working on my car, but it kept getting worse. Now, I've completely pulled away from everything and just sit in my chair all day, letting calls go to voicemail.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if these feelings of emptiness, guilt, and hearing the voice have been present every day for the past four months, or have there been any periods where you felt slightly better or more like your old self?\n\nPatient: Yes, they have been there every single day for the last four months, without any breaks or times where I felt like my old self. It all started a few weeks after the cardiologist's diagnosis and has just been one continuous, heavy dark spell since then.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice you hear and the thoughts about your heart being punished by God relate to each other, and do you ever have times when you question whether these beliefs are real or not?\n\nPatient: The voice and my thoughts are deeply connected because it tells me exactly what I already believe—that my heart is rotten and God is finished with me as punishment for my past mistakes. It is almost impossible for me to doubt it because the voice sounds so incredibly real, and I find myself answering it out loud and begging it to be wrong.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever have moments where you're able to step back and think that maybe the voice and your beliefs about your heart being punished by God might not be true, or are you completely convinced of their reality at all times?\n\nPatient: I am completely convinced because the voice sounds just as clear and real as you talking to me right now. Even though it terrifies me and I beg it to be wrong, I truly believe my heart is failing as a punishment from God.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there are any times when the voice tells you something that isn't related to your heart or your feelings of guilt and punishment, or if it's always focused on those specific themes?\n\nPatient: No, it never talks about anything else; it is always focused on those exact same things. It only ever tells me that my heart is rotten, that God is finished with me, and that my heart is just going to stop.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever experience any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see anything unusual or have any other kinds of hallucinations. It's only that deep, clear voice I hear over my shoulder, especially at night when the house gets quiet.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe that the voice you hear is a direct message from God, or do you think it might be something else, like your own mind trying to make sense of your situation?\n\nPatient: It feels like a direct, punishing message from God because of how terrifyingly real and external it sounds. I can't believe it's just my own mind playing tricks on me when it's so loud and clear, which is why I end up begging it to be wrong.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how you distinguish between the voice's messages about your heart and your own thoughts about being a burden and feeling guilty, or do they feel like the same thing to you?\n\nPatient: They feel closely connected, but they sound very different to me. The voice is a physical, external sound right over my shoulder telling me my heart is rotten and God is finished with me, which is so real I actually talk back to it. My feelings of guilt and being a burden are more like heavy, quiet thoughts I've gotten into my own head, making me believe everyone would be better off if I just disappeared.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a moment when the voice told you something about your heart that wasn't related to your guilt or punishment, or is it always tied to those feelings of guilt and being a burden?\n\nPatient: No, there has never been a moment like that; the voice is always tied directly to those feelings of guilt and punishment. It never makes neutral comments, but instead tells me that my heart is rotten and God is finished with me. It just constantly reinforces the feeling that I am being punished and that I'm a burden.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the voice you hear and the feelings of guilt and being a burden started at the same time, or did one begin before the other?\n\nPatient: The heavy depression and feelings of guilt definitely started first. I had already sunk into this dark, heavy spell where I couldn't even get out of bed or care about anything before the voice ever showed up. It genuinely feels like a punishment from God and that my heart is truly giving out, so it's hard to just see it as a symptom.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times when the voice or your beliefs about being punished might be trying to make sense of your difficult emotions or situation, rather than being a direct message from God or an absolute fact?\n\nPatient: I can see why you'd ask that, and it's true that none of this started until after I fell into this deep, dark depression.
